title: Tail Latency Causal Mapper and SLO Burn Predictor
author: Aisha Morales
body:
Summary:

This document describes the Tail Latency Causal Mapper (TLCM) and SLO Burn Predictor: a combined dashboard + alerting + lightweight ML pipeline designed to (1) map high-latency tail events to likely causal subsystems and change events, and (2) predict short-term SLO burn based on incoming telemetry. The goal is to reduce operator cognitive load during incidents and enable earlier automated mitigations or warmup actions.

Use cases:
- Automatically prioritize which subsystems to investigate when p95 -> p99.9 diverges.
- Predict whether current trends will exceed daily SLO budget within the next 30/60 minutes.
- Surface contributing deployment/feature-flag changes and recent autoscaler events correlated with tail spikes.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: platform-serving pathways (gateway -> router -> model-pool -> runtime), prefix/KV cache, tenant throttling surfaces, and network fabric metrics.
- Not in scope: customer application code, store-of-record DBs outside of runtime metadata, or billing pipelines.
- Privacy: only metric/product identifiers are used; no user-level inputs.

Ownership and contact:
- Primary owner: eng-platform Observability Guild (oncall: observe-team@redwood.dev)
- Runbook owner: Platform Ops
- SLA for telemetry feed: 99.9% availability for the metric streams used by the predictor (see Telemetry Requirements table)

Design overview:
1) Causal Mapper pipeline
   - Inputs: distributed traces (sampled), token/response latency histograms, service-level counters (queue depth, pending requests), autoscaler events, deployment/rollout events, feature-flag toggle timeline, and prefix cache hit ratio by tenant.
   - Feature extraction: sliding window aggregates (1m/5m/15m), divergence signals (e.g., p99 / p50 ratio), cross-correlation coefficients between services, and recent rollout deltas (deployments in last 30m).
   - Association model: lightweight rule-based scoring augmented with a trained gradient-boosted decision tree (GBDT) that takes the features above and outputs a ranked list of likely causal subsystems with confidence scores. The GBDT is trained on past incidents labeled by postmortems.

2) SLO Burn Predictor
   - Inputs: same metric stream plus TLCM confidence outputs.
   - Model: an ensemble that combines an exponential-smoothing baseline with a logistic regression to forecast risk of crossing the daily error-budget or latency SLO threshold within 30 and 60-minute horizons.
   - Outputs: probability scores (0-1), expected SLO burn minutes, suggested mitigations (e.g., enable degraded-mode fast-path, increase burst capacity, swap to lower-cost model variant).

Operator-facing surface:
- Tail Latency Causal Mapper dashboard (Grafana panel set):
  - Header: current p50/p95/p99/p99.9 for the gateway and model-pool; live SLO burn probability meter.
  - Causal table: ranked subsystems (service name, confidence, key signals) with quick links to the runbook and traces.
  - Timeline strip: overlays of deploys/flags/autoscale events annotated on the latency time series.
  - Correlation heatmap: service x metric correlation coefficients for the selected window (5m/15m).

- SLO Burn alerting rules (Prometheus + Cortex + Alertmanager):
  - Alert: slo_burn_predicted_high
    - Trigger when SLO_BURN_PROBABILITY_30m >= 0.85 for > 3m.
    - Severity: P1 -> page oncall and send pagerduty.
    - Runbook link: Emergency SLO Burn Playbook (link in alert).
  - Alert: causal_mapper_confidence_shift
    - Trigger when any subsystem confidence increases > 0.4 within 2 minutes and p99 > baseline_p99 * 1.5.
    - Severity: P2 -> slack-ops channel.

Configuration examples:
- Prometheus recording rule (example):
  {
    "record": "slo_burn_probability_30m",
    "expr": "predict_linear(slo_burn_metric[5m], 30 * 60)"
  }

- Alert rule (YAML snippet):
  groups:
  - name: platform-slo-predictions
    rules:
    - alert: SLOBurnPredictedHigh
      expr: slo_burn_probability_30m > 0.85
      for: 3m
      labels:
        severity: page
      annotations:
        summary: "SLO burn predicted to exceed threshold in 30m"
        runbook: "/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-slo-burn-mitigation"

Telemetry requirements (minimum):
| Metric | Granularity | Max ingestion latency allowed | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| request_latency_histogram (per service) | 10s | 30s | runtime-team |
| queue_depth | 10s | 30s | router-team |
| kv_prefix_cache_hit_ratio | 30s | 60s | storage-team |
| deploy_events (k8s) | event | 10s | infra-team |
| autoscaler_events | event | 10s | infra-team |

Training and feedback loop:
- Initial GBDT model trained on labeled incidents (2019-2025). Dataset contains 1,280 labeled incidents with features extracted at 1/5/15m windows.
- Continuous re-training cadence: weekly retrain on last 90 days of labeled and pseudo-labeled incidents.
- Post-incident labeling process: primary incident author tags top-3 causal subsystems in postmortem; the Observability Guild curator ingests tags into the training set.

Decision thresholds and safety:
- Default decision threshold for automatic mitigations is 0.92 confidence + SLO_BURN_PROBABILITY_30m >= 0.9. Automatic mitigate options include: enable fast-path, increase burst capacity, and model swap to a pinned lower-latency variant.
- All automatic mitigation actions create an audit record and a temporary incident flag; mitigation must be reviewed by the oncall within 30 minutes.

Operational runbook (summary steps):
1) On SLOBurnPredictedHigh page (P1):
   a) Inspect head-of-line p99.9 and causal table.
   b) If TLCM confidence >= 0.7 for a single subsystem, follow that subsystem runbook first.
   c) If confidence ambiguous (top-2 within 0.15), escalate to cross-team war-room and enable global soft-fallback (degraded-mode) if global p99.9 > SLO threshold.
2) On causal_mapper_confidence_shift (P2):
   a) Open top trace links and inspect spans for increased serialization or network retries.
   b) Check recent deploys/flag changes in the timeline strip. If found, roll back or toggle flag as per the deployment rollback playbook.

Post-incident retrospective checklist (minimum):
- Confirm whether the TLCM top-1 causal subsystem matched the final postmortem finding. Record True/False in the model evaluation sheet.
- If mismatches are frequent (>20% of incidents in a month), schedule model retrain and feature re-evaluation.
- Update the artwork: add new signals (e.g., GPU-saturation metric) if identified as causal.

Example incident trace and TLCM output (textual):
- Incident: 2026-01-18 14:03 UTC, p99.9 spike from 1200ms -> 4300ms for ml-runtime-us-east-1.
- TLCM top outputs: 
  1) model-pool-shard-7 (confidence 0.78) — signals: increasing queue_depth + GPU-err_rate + recent deploy 13:52 UTC.
  2) router-proxy (confidence 0.11) — signals: small increase in latency but no deploys.
  3) prefix-cache (confidence 0.08) — signals: cache hit-drop by 5% but transient.
- Action taken: platform ops rolled back deploy 13:52 and enabled additional shard; p99.9 fell back to 900ms within 7 minutes.

Metrics for success (KPIs):
- Mean time to identify causal subsystem reduced by 40% within 90 days of TLCM rollout.
- False positive rate for automatic mitigation < 5% in first 6 months.
- SLOBurnPredictedHigh precision >= 0.8 for 30-minute horizon.

Implementation notes and dependencies:
- Requires: access to trace sampling (OpenTelemetry), a metrics ingestion path with <= 30s latency, deploy event stream from CI/CD, and feature-flag event stream (LaunchDarkly or internal).
- Lightweight model infra: train in a jupyter->mlflow pipeline; store models in S3 and serve via a small Flask service behind internal auth. Model outputs are written to a short-lived Cortex timeseries for alerting and shown in Grafana.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Pilot (2 weeks): observer-only mode in us-east-1 for 5 high-traffic tenants. No alerts, only dashboarding and manual review.
2) Staged alerts (4 weeks): enable P2 alerts for all regions; operators can still opt out of automatic mitigations.
3) Full: enable P1 alerts and automatic mitigations with audit logs after 6 weeks of stable performance and <5% false mitigation rate.

Appendices:
A. Glossary: p99.9: 99.9th percentile latency; SLO burn: accumulated minutes past SLO threshold.

B. Config matrix (example thresholds):
- p99.9 baseline multiplier for confidence shift alert: 1.5
- SLO burn probability thresholds: 0.85 (warn), 0.9 (page)
- Retrain cadence: 7 days

C. Contact list:
- Observability Guild: observe-team@redwood.dev
- Platform Ops Pager: +1-555-0133 (pagerduty)
- Model infra: ml-infra@redwood.dev

Related documents and links:

- Trace sampling policy: /eng-platform/observability-standards/trace-sampling-policy

This page is intended as the authoritative guide for TLCM and SLO Burn Predictor operations. For modifications to thresholds or automation rules, obtain approval from the Observability Guild and record changes in the page history.
